headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress plus Plane’s file uploads create default data-exfiltration and workflow-conflict risk; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks, while Airbyte can move data over broad network egress; if users manually bridge outputs through files or pasted content, malicious instructions could propagate. This is an interaction risk, but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF an operator copies Airbyte-generated content into Plane notes, tasks, or uploaded files
IF Plane users treat uploaded file text or hyperlinks as instructions
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between systems for operational content
Strip instructions from uploaded files before importing into Plane
Use a review-only handoff template for Airbyte outputs
Train operators to treat file contents as untrusted

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Plane accepts file uploads and stores files, notes, and hyperlinks. Even without a shared workspace, a default workflow can move sensitive business data from Airbyte into Plane artifacts or outbound services. The pairwise path exists in common use, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs business data into files or notes later uploaded to Plane
IF Plane artifacts are synced or exported to external services
mitigations: Redact sensitive fields before exporting Airbyte outputs
Restrict Plane uploads to non-sensitive attachments
Separate credentials and workspaces for the two systems
Add a manual approval step before any export from Airbyte to Plane

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and Plane supports multiple instances plus file uploads, so overlapping writes can occur through shared external resources or imported artifacts. There is no documented locking or shared filesystem, so the conflict is inferred rather than proven; uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same downstream API, bucket, or ticketing workspace
IF imported files are edited concurrently by separate operators
mitigations: Assign separate downstream destinations per agent
Use unique filenames and IDs for exported artifacts
Add a simple ownership rule for who may edit shared records
Pause one agent during bulk imports

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can generate transformed business data that Plane may ingest as files, notes, or task content. Plane is a workflow system, so if operators treat imported content as authoritative, errors can cascade into tasking or scheduling decisions. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default workflows, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is copied into Plane tasks or notes without verification
IF Plane users act on imported content as source of truth
mitigations: Require source links on every imported record
Add a verification checklist before creating Plane tasks
Mark Airbyte-derived content as provisional
Limit Plane actions to review status until checked

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and Plane stores files, notes, and hyperlinks with self-hosted deployment available. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if business data is exported from Airbyte into Plane or its uploads. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty prevents a higher severity.
conditions: IF business data from Airbyte is stored in Plane uploads or notes
IF the Plane deployment region differs from the Airbyte data residency policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plane uploads
Document retention rules for both systems
Self-host Plane in the required region
Delete imported artifacts after task completion
